A useful sceptical frame to hold next to the Anthropic Riemann result the same day.

tail.title: People keep sending me AI slop that they want me to post on the blog
tail.summary: Gelman's complaint in full: people send him chatbot output rather than the prompt that produced it, and he would rather have the prompt. The implicit methodological point is that the prompt is the information-bearing artifact and the completion is derivative, which is the same reason eval papers that publish outputs without prompts are unreproducible. Two sentences long and correct.

tail.title: I caught my students using AI to cheat in an exam - here's what universities must do
tail.summary: A first-person account of detecting AI use in an examination setting and a set of institutional prescriptions that follow from it. The interesting part for eval people is the detection basis, since individual-case AI-attribution claims almost never survive scrutiny at the standard a disciplinary process requires. Runs alongside the Danish policy of requiring verbal defence of written assignments.

tail.title: The tragedy of the commons, AI edition
tail.summary: On the collective-action failure created by AI crawlers and agents consuming freely-provided public web resources at a rate the providers cannot sustain — the same dynamic that just forced Gentoo's Bugzilla offline. The framing is that no individual scraper is acting irrationally, which is precisely why voluntary restraint will not fix it. Paywalled.

tail.title: AI fortunes are reviving an old debate about private power
tail.summary: On the concentration of AI wealth into a small number of private philanthropic vehicles and the Gilded Age precedent for what happens when private fortunes start setting public research agendas. Relevant to independent researchers because the same concentration shows up on the funding side as evaluator and grantmaker concentration. Commentary, not reporting.

tail.title: Why normal people aren't using AI agents
tail.summary: On the gap between agent capability demos and actual consumer adoption, and why the tasks agents are best at are not the tasks most people want automated. Worth reading as a corrective if your sense of adoption comes from HN and developer Twitter. Could not fetch the full text from this machine; summary is from the headline and surrounding coverage.

tail.title: An AI-native finance function: five lessons from OpenAI's CFO
tail.summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar's five lessons on rebuilding a finance function around AI, covering automated forecasting, control design and how they measure AI ROI internally. Vendor content about its own deployment, so treat the ROI claims as marketing. Included for the controls angle rather than the numbers.

tail.title: OpenAI's letter to Governor Abbott on responsible AI infrastructure in Texas
tail.summary: OpenAI's public letter to the Texas governor committing to 'reliable, transparent' datacentre growth in the state. Notable mainly as a datapoint in the emerging pattern of labs negotiating directly with state governments over siting and power, which is where AI energy policy is actually being decided. No technical content.

tail.title: Premium seats are coming to ChatGPT Business
tail.summary: A pricing-tier announcement adding premium seats with higher usage limits to ChatGPT Business, with $100 in workspace credits for signups before 20 August. Included only because API and seat-pricing changes propagate into pipeline costs. Skip unless you run a team workspace.

tail.title: Model ML completes finance work more efficiently with GPT-5.6 Sol
tail.summary: A customer case study on Model ML using GPT-5.6 Sol to carry finance work from research through to editable, traceable PowerPoint and Excel artifacts. The one transferable idea is the insistence on traceability in the generated deliverable rather than just the answer. Otherwise vendor marketing.

tail.title: Mistral patent for 'code implemented tool calls'
tail.summary: A granted US patent to Mistral covering tool calls expressed as executable code rather than structured JSON — the pattern now used by essentially every agent framework, including Claude Code's own tool-use path. The HN thread is mostly about whether the claims are broad enough to be enforceable against open-source implementations. Worth knowing exists if you ship an agent framework.

tail.title: The future is for everyone: Meta's path to a positive AI future
tail.summary: Meta's positioning document accompanying its return to open-weight releases, arguing distribution of capability is the safety strategy. It is the manifesto half of the Muse Glimmer launch and should be read as advocacy. Useful as a primary source for how the open-weights case is being made at the largest scale.

tail.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 hits 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with a public harness
tail.summary: A third-party evaluation putting DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 at 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, with the harness published rather than described. The public-harness part is the reason to care: most vendor agentic-benchmark claims are unreproducible because the scaffold is the uncontrolled variable. Verify the harness before citing the number.

tail.title: DeepSeek costs an OpenCode Go user $1.14/day; dual DGX breaks even in 24 years
tail.summary: A back-of-envelope that has been circulating: at observed usage a heavy agentic-coding user spends about $1.14/day on DeepSeek inference, against which a dual-DGX local rig takes roughly 24 years to break even. The point is that the local-inference economic case now rests on privacy, latency and control rather than cost. Directly relevant if you are sizing local hardware against API spend.

tail.title: GitHub Models is now retired
tail.summary: GitHub has completed the retirement of GitHub Models, its unified playground and API across multiple LLM providers; Willison found out when a scheduled Actions run in his research repo failed with a brownout message. His post-mortem is that it was an odd-shaped product without a clear owner. Check any CI that hits the GitHub Models endpoint.

tail.title: Quoting the Claude Opus 5 system prompt on the Fable/Mythos export-control suspension
tail.summary: The Opus 5 system prompt contains an explicit post-cutoff briefing: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 released 9 June 2026, access suspended 12 June to comply with US Commerce export controls, controls lifted 30 June, access restored 1 July. The mechanism is interesting on its own — Anthropic is patching known post-training-cutoff facts in via the system prompt rather than retraining. Useful precedent if you are reasoning about what a model 'knows' versus what it was told at inference.

tail.title: SQLite compressed text-history prototypes
tail.summary: Willison prototypes storing document revision history as a JSON array of every prior version, zlib/zstd-compressed as one blob, on the theory that the massive string repetition compresses away. Notable methodologically for how it was built — dictated to GPT-Live voice mode while walking the dog. A small, concrete example of the research-prototype loop rather than a finished result.

tail.title: 5 useful things you'll learn in my new post-training textbook
tail.summary: Lambert's RLHF book is out through Manning as 'Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: Aligning and Post-training LLMs', grown out of the open website he maintained while training open models. This post is the five-things pitch for what is in it. The open web version remains the reference most post-training work cites.

tail.title: I got an email about resistance
tail.summary: Goedecke publishes in full a reader's critique — that he concedes deep-thinking software work is ending, admits it saddens him, and then counsels acceptance anyway — along with his reply. It is the most articulate version of the 'why aren't you resisting this' objection to pragmatist AI commentary. Worth reading for the argument structure rather than the conclusion.

tail.title: Open Thread 446
tail.summary: The weekly ACX open thread. This week's comment-of-the-week highlights FutureSearch founder Dan Schwarz on what the correlation between forecasting accuracy and time horizon implies about a ceiling on forecastability. Relevant if you follow the AI-forecasting-evaluation literature.

tail.title: AI-based multimodal integration of genomics and electronic health records
tail.summary: A review of methods combining genomic data with EHR records under one model, and the validation problems that follow when the two modalities carry different and correlated demographic biases. Relevant to clinical-LLM audit work because EHR-derived labels are the ground truth most clinical evaluations quietly rely on. Review, not new results.

tail.title: The Transformative AI Fund's application form still carries the old fund's name in its URL
tail.summary: Operational detail worth knowing before applying: the live application link published on the Transformative AI Fund page is a Paperform URL whose query string still reads fund=Long-Term%20Future%20Fund. The form was re-pointed rather than rebuilt, so landing on a page that says Long-Term Future Fund is not evidence you have the wrong link. It also means aggregators keying off the old name will keep looking correct while describing a fund that no longer exists.

tail.title: AAAI-27 will take workshop proposals until 28 August with no affiliation gate - a venue route that needs no finished paper
tail.summary: NEW TO THIS BOARD. Proposals close Friday 28 August AoE (UTC-12) with notification 25 September, for workshops held 22-23 February 2027 in Montreal. A proposal is about 2 pages and not more than 4, covering topic, timeliness, organiser expertise, format and duration, with no affiliation requirement stated. The real constraint is social rather than institutional: the call wants an organising committee of ideally three or four people knowledgeable in the field, so this is only reachable with co-organisers - but for someone with no institution it is one of the few ways to hold venue standing without a completed empirical paper.

tail.title: Coefficient Giving also runs a Century Fellowship, but it 403s like the rest of the domain
tail.summary: Surfaced in the same domain-restricted search as the career funding page and previously unseen on this board: Coefficient runs a Century Fellowship and a separate RFP on Effective Careers alongside the technical safety and capability-evaluations RFPs already tracked. A direct fetch returned HTTP 403 like every other page on the domain, so nothing about amount, duration, eligibility or status can be stated. Recorded so a future run picks it up with a domain-restricted search rather than rediscovering it, not as an actionable item.

tail.title: UWA's fee offset is competitive, not paired — the stipend and the tuition waiver are two separate lotteries
tail.summary: Re-verified on UWA's own HDR scholarships page and the fee position is now explicit enough to downgrade. The 2027 International RTP Stipend and Tuition Fee Scholarships round opened 1 August 2026 at 9.00am AWST and closes 15 September 2026 at 11.59pm AWST — 35 days — with ranking in October, offers from November and commencement February to March 2027. The stipend 'current value in 2026 is $38,110 per annum'. But the tuition instrument is described as awarded 'to a limited number of international students, via a competitive selection process' rather than automatically alongside the stipend, so a stipend offer does not imply a fee waiver. UWA policy separately confirms an RTP fees offset 'pays for the tuition fees for the duration of the course, up to a maximum of four years full-time equivalent study for a doctorate' — generous when won, but winning it is a second competition. OSHC is not mentioned on any UWA page reached this run, and an askUWA enquiry page explicitly declines to address it. Supervisor is a soft gate: UWA instructs applicants to choose a course and supervisor before applying but publishes no signed-agreement requirement. Minimum entry qualification is still not published anywhere reachable.

tail.title: Melbourne's 31 October figure comes back, this time from the right page — but it is still index-derived and unimelb still 403s everything
tail.summary: PARTIAL REHABILITATION of a figure this board downgraded yesterday, obtained by abandoning the central scholarships page and targeting the course page instead. A domain-restricted index pass on the Doctor of Philosophy (Engineering and IT) 'How to apply' page returns that applications close 31 October for international applicants applying for graduate research scholarships — the same number as before, but sourced from the correct per-course page rather than the deferred-candidate snippet that produced it last time. Melbourne's own wording still says published closing dates 'aren't usually different for domestic and international applications' and that international applicants should apply earlier for visa and scholarship assessment. Package, confirmed a fourth way: living allowance $39,500 per year pro rata (2026 full-time rate) for up to 3.5 years, FULL fee offset for up to four years for internationals, plus OSHC and relocation, with more than 300 awards to international graduate researchers annually and automatic consideration with no separate scholarship form. VERIFICATION STATUS UNCHANGED AND POOR: study.unimelb.edu.au, scholarships.unimelb.edu.au and the course page itself all 403 WebFetch. The browser pane is 3-for-3 on timeouts and was not attempted. Treat 31 October as a working assumption, not a verified date.

deadlines.note: Remote, no geography or affiliation requirement, 5-40 hrs/week, 230+ mentors. Blocker: verbatim UNPAID, down to the mentor level, and it runs to 14 December — a straight trade-off against AIAF, not a second shot.

deadlines.note: $39,220 tax-free for 3.5 years + tuition + Single OSHC — a complete package. This is the OPENING date, newly page-verified. It matters more than the 19 Oct close because you cannot self-nominate: an enrolling school must put you forward, which needs supervisor lead time.

deadlines.note: 8,000-word guideline, no hard page cap, archival in the ACM DL. Blocker is upstream: without the 13 August abstract registered there is no paper submission.

deadlines.note: 7 pages main content, 9 max with references past page 7, cannot be transferred from the main track. Same missing-portal blocker as the abstract.

deadlines.note: $15-25M round. Funds INDIVIDUALS, for-profits and non-US applicants with no 501(c)(3) requirement, and supplies fiscal sponsorship where the work qualifies — which is the recurring blocker solved. Also runs direct grants funded in 1-2 weeks, not only the October cycle.

deadlines.label: Corrigibility Research Fund — round one closes
deadlines.note: No eligibility criteria of any kind published, no fiscal sponsor needed, no country restriction. Apply by short email to grants@corrigibilityresearch.org. The lowest-friction application on the entire board.

deadlines.label: BlackboxNLP 2026 — ARR commitment deadline
deadlines.note: Interpretability and explanation workshop at EMNLP, archival in the ACL Anthology — a strong topical fit. Blocker is absolute: commitment requires reviews from an ARR cycle you did not submit to. Listed so the route is not mistaken for open.

deadlines.note: $35,656 + GUIPRS tuition + OSHC for 57 months explicitly included — a complete package, and international closes a week BEFORE domestic. NEW DISCREPANCY this run: GUIPRS tuition cover now reads 'up to three years' where it previously read 3.5, which would leave ~6 months of unfunded international tuition. Worth one email.

deadlines.label: AAAI-27 workshop proposals due
deadlines.note: NEW this run. 2-4 page proposal, no affiliation requirement stated, workshops run 22-23 Feb 2027 in Montreal, notification 25 September. A route to venue standing that needs no finished paper — the blocker is social (co-organisers), not institutional.

deadlines.label: NeurIPS 2026 TAE — 'Can We Trust AI Evaluation?' (SYDNEY)
deadlines.note: Up to 8 pages excluding references, non-archival, double-blind, no fee or affiliation gate stated. Held 11-12 December in SYDNEY — the one major venue reachable without international travel. Gated on the OpenReview account.

deadlines.note: 6-page full / 4-page short / 2-page Junior Spotlight, non-archival with opt-out, portal open since 1 August. deadlines.note: $35,886 pro rata under Dr Joshua Newn — the closest topical match on the AU board to your XAI/human-trust work. THE PAGE SAYS 30 SEPTEMBER: that is RMIT's DOMESTIC date; international is 30 August. Carries a rare equivalence clause — 'unless supervisor provides a case for equivalence' — a human-judgement route around the honours floor. Fees/OSHC not stated at project level.

deadlines.note: $40,475 + International Student Fees + full OSHC INCLUDING IMMEDIATE FAMILY. An H2A candidate could win the stipend and still pay full fees. No separate application — ask ANU before 31 Aug. International closes TWO MONTHS before domestic.

deadlines.note: AN OPENING, NOT A DUE DATE. AURS/RTPS gives a stipend (no figure published), a 100% tuition fee waiver, relocation support and OSHC. Nothing is advertised yet — this is a watch item, not an action item.

deadlines.note: RESOLVED after four runs of 'not open'. $19.2k stipend + $24k compute, Berkeley or London in person, and the page now states J1 VISA COVERED IF NEEDED plus travel — the standing blocker is gone. Two cautions: mech-interp is adjacent to rather than centred on your work, and an EA Forum post says 29 Aug for the same stream — work to the earlier date. /stream/nanda 404s; use /apply.

deadlines.note: Proceedings 8pp archival in PMLR, Findings 4pp. Sydney 6-7 December, so domestic travel only. Registration cost is stated as 'forthcoming', so do not record it as free.

deadlines.note: Single hard gate, no separate abstract, notification 17 December, Pittsburgh 10-14 May 2027. Blocker: collides exactly with ML4H, and CHI is the more expensive commitment. Fee and affiliation text is absent from the site — labelled unverified, not absent.

deadlines.note: $42,754 + 100% tuition for up to 14 research periods + OSHC + relocation and thesis allowances — fees and health both confirmed in writing, which most doors do not do. Blocker: two-part submission (admission + scholarship) and first-class honours or a research masters.

deadlines.note: $38,110. DOWNGRADED 11 Aug: the tuition instrument is awarded 'to a limited number of international students, via a competitive selection process' — a SECOND competition, not a pairing with the stipend as the 10 Aug board recorded. OSHC still silent. Supervisor is a soft gate.

deadlines.note: Reciprocal-review exemption confirmed for authors with no qualifying publication, capped at one such paper per author — but it lives on /AuthorGuidelines, not the CFP, so a CFP-only read reports no exemption. Gated on the OpenReview account.

deadlines.note: NEW DOOR, and one of only three written down to upper-second honours — verified verbatim: 'Honours degree (First Class or Second Class Upper) or equivalent'. USyd RTP rate $42,754 for 3 years + $2,500/yr conference funding + academic course fees and SSAF for internationals over 12 research periods. Closes 'once suitable recipients have been identified'. Gates: unconditional PhD offer in Engineering, Sydney AI Centre affiliation, fundamental AI research. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the RTP round. OSHC unstated.

BUT: 'Tuition fees are not covered' — not a funded door standing alone. It does partially restore the stackable-top-up assumption the 410-Gone Data61 pages destroyed.

deadlines.note: CORRECTED THIS RUN and verified directly — NOT course-gated. Average decision within a day, 9 in 10 answered within a week. The fastest money on the board.

deadlines.note: REPLACES the Long-Term Future Fund, which EA Funds has closed — verified on the fund index directly. deadlines.note: Read on METR's own page, not an index. Contractor structure sidesteps the work-rights question the Working Holiday Visa raises, and remote means location-agnostic. METR builds capability evaluations — the closest commercial analogue to your three audits.
